coverage: An ordinary authenticated user receives 403 from the management plan route before a review is created.
A demoted user receives 403 from the management commit route even with a previously valid plan and idempotency key.
Ordinary users also receive 403 from operation progress; anonymous access receives 401 and creates no operation.
The same typed install/update/action plan route is used for management review, so role enforcement does not depend on frontend controls.
An ungranted reader receives an empty directory; administrators receive no implicit audience bypass.
OU ancestry grants access only through the current group creation identity and current membership topology. Reparenting, stale creation identity, zero identity and cycles fail closed.
Two disjoint restricted OU readers each list exactly their own one report; direct IDs from the other OU return 404 without leaking content.
Launch inspection and directory routes deny ungranted, stale-generation and no-access readers without exposing hidden installation metadata.
A denied optional network capability cannot sign or dispatch a direct request, releases no response and does not mutate authority state.
Optional capabilities are not implicitly granted. An undeclared or invalid selection is refused.
An unsupported required capability is refused by package staging/capability selection before installation admission.
Missing or mismatched runtime profiles for a required provider are refused instead of being synthesized.
Role demotion, inactive account, expired/revoked session, changed session revision and deleted/recreated username invalidate the next actor/launch check rather than inheriting prior authority.
Moving an account between OUs changes the authority fingerprint without changing lifecycle identity. Deleted/recreated users and OUs cannot resurrect access grants.
Replacing an OU after review creation makes commit return 409 and creates no operation.
Deleted/recreated/inactive/expired audience principals and changed OU creation identities are refused with no persistent mutation.
Wrong app ID, wrong generation, stale policy/capability policy, inactive/expired account, session-revision mismatch and invalid installation IDs are refused before launch metadata is exposed.
Viewer derivation rejects revoked/expired sessions, changed account generation, removed grants, stale OU identity, corrupt/missing identity keys and restore pause.
Backend request signing derives viewer authority from the current host account; app-supplied role/subject fields do not become the execution viewer.
Writable and managed request tests fence policy/account drift before response consumption.
Changing a capability grant while install staging is pending refuses the stage and leaves durable state unchanged.
A pending required grant cannot become active; exact capability row/policy/review changes are refused at commit.

Credential rotation revokes the old binding until explicit reapproval, and credential revocation invalidates the current use immediately. Stale binding review after network-policy drift writes no row.
Writable request binding rejects generation, policy and release drift before dispatch.
Missing or malformed native provenance is classified as uncertain, releases no response and is not automatically retried.
The native artifact records revocation before and after an actual external IO boundary, post-IO OU revocation, uncertain no-retry and owned cleanup.
Background service assertions contain no user identity and cannot impersonate a user.
Every use rechecks current installation generation, policy revision, background capability grant and restore pause.
Disable, generation change, policy drift, grant removal and restored state invalidate the service assertion.
A background probe cannot submit after revocation and cannot claim results under a stale service identity.

limits: These are development server/API tests, not the complete H16 machine matrix, capacity benchmark or manual browser review.
AUTH-08 and the remaining SEC/RUN/LIFE rows are outside this evidence increment.
